answer: Sybil resistance here is a capital threshold applied per identity: each account must lock a non-transferable bond, so N clones cost N stakes, not one stake reused N times. Weight earns only when it also matches measurable work, so idle clones drain instead of compound. Copper-tier attackers can fund a few clones, so each bond is paired with per-epoch attestation that exposes extra identities. The canyon between honest and attacker cost curves is the target: a farm pays per mouth and stays locked, so each marginal identity costs more than it extracts. Marble is the base stake unit per identity.
